source_text: Iam vero "de Ioseph, cuius Mariam" teste Evangelio "coniugem" dixi [n112] , multa diu disputas contra sententiam meam, et conaris ostendere, "quia concubitus defuit, nullo modo fuisse coniugium" … Non ergo quia dixi omne nuptiarum, id est, hoc tripartitum bonum, in illis Christi parentibus fuisse completum; propterea hoc dixisse putari debeo, sicut insimulas, "ut quidquid aliter fuerit, malum esse videatur".
pass_a_gloss: Now truly 'about Joseph, whose Mary', with the Gospel as witness, 'wife' I said, many things for long you dispute against my opinion, and you try to show 'because lying-together was lacking, in no way to have been a marriage'. — Not therefore because I said the whole (good) of marriage, that is, this threefold good, in those parents of Christ to have been fulfilled, on that account ought I to be thought to have said this, as you accuse, 'so that whatever was otherwise may seem to be evil'.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “Now, as for Joseph, whose ‘wife’ I called Mary on the testimony of the Gospel, you argue long and at length against my view, and you try to show ‘that, because intercourse was absent, it was in no way a marriage.’”

“So I ought not to be thought, just because I said that the whole good of marriage, that is, this threefold good, was fulfilled in those parents of Christ, to have said it, as you falsely charge, ‘so that whatever was otherwise would seem to be evil.’”

choices.why: Opening fides promissionis is the pledge of a promise, not the theological virtue.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
